newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB start merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft, NordLB start merger talks.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG and regional bank Norddeutsche Landesbank on Wednesday announced they were beginning merger talks which could create one of the country's largest banking groups.

The banks said a working party of management and their federal state owners had proposed fusing NordLB into a group led by Bankgesellschaft as early as mid-1998, pending talks due for completion this year.

"The merger ... aims to form a banking group whose size, competence and flexibility can meet the demands of the future and which can also hold a leading position in its core regions amid the expected changes in the banking landscape," a joint statement said.

Combined, Bankgesellschaft and NordLB would have total assets of more than 500 billion marks, larger than Commerzbank AG, the third largest commercial bank and on a par with Westdeutsche Landesbank, the leader in the public sector.

Talks are expected to be completed in 1997, allowing the merger to go ahead in the middle of next year -- a major step forward from the limited co-operation talks the banks have been holding since last year.
"We are all agreed on the basic structure of the plan," said Bankgesellschaft spokeswoman Rita Ackermann-Jakli.
"The main step now is that valuations have been commissioned (of both banks) and these will play a major role in the discussions," she added.
The new group would be partly owned by the public sector and partly remain in private hands, the banks said, without giving details.
Bankgesellshaft is currently 56 percent owned by the city state of Berlin while NordLB is owned by three different federal states, mainly Lower Saxony.
Bankgesellschaft's shares, much in demand like the whole German banking sector, hit a year high of 38 marks after the news and closed up 42 pfennigs, or 1.2 percent, at 37.90.

Investors have been eager for merger news in German banking ever since Deutsche Bank AG revealed a 5.21 percent stake in rival Bayerische Vereinsbank AG last summer, sparking a frenzy of takeover speculation.
If it goes ahead, the Bankgesllschaft-NordLB merger will mark the first significant fusion in an overcrowded industry widely viewed as over-ripe for consolidation.

"In principle, this is a rather positive thing, although there are some points of concern," said BHF-Bank analyst Dieter Hein, who said the merger could raise the proportion of public sector ownership of Bankgesellschaft to 85 percent.
"The fact that a merger would bring a focus more on public sector activities is a worry, as these are not exactly consistent with dynamic banking services," Hein said.

Bankgesellschaft, currently undergoing a wide restructuring process under a new management headed by chairman Wolfgang Rupf, aims to keep at least 40 percent of shares in the new bank in private hands, the spokeswoman said.
The merger envisaged would create a bank headed by Bankgesellschaft but headquartered in both Berlin and Hanover, where NordLB is based.
NordLB would become an independent unit of that group, along with Bankgesellschaft's existing units, Landesbank Berlin, Berliner Bank and Berliner Hannoversche Hypothekenbank.

Investment banking activities, highlighted by Bankgesellschaft last year as a problematic strategic area, would be concentrated at the parent company, along with major corporate clients and foreign business.
The remaining units will retain responsibility for their own areas, such as retail and mortgage business and specialist public sector banking activities.
Bankgesellschaft's current overhaul plan will include shedding 10 percent of its 17,000 staff in 1997 and 1998 and closing branch offices.
The bank reported a 90 percent slump in 1996 net profit due to a steep increase in loan loss provisions but said its earnings should recover this year.
